THE WORK, EXPLAINED

Make room for what comes next.

A stump can interrupt mowing, occupy space in a planting bed, or hold up the next stage of a yard project. Grinding reduces the stump in the agreed work area and leaves a mixture of wood chips and soil. It is different from digging out the stump and its entire root system.

Tell us how you plan to use the area afterward. Grass, a new planting, and a construction project can call for different preparation. We will discuss the grinding area and depth before quoting; soil replacement, sod, and additional root work need their own agreed scope.

What affects stump grinding cost in Houston?

The width at ground level, root flare, number of stumps, access, grinding depth, and handling of the grindings all affect the estimate. A narrow gate or a stump next to a fence needs a different plan from an open front yard. Send photos of both the stump and the equipment route so we can review the whole job.

BEFORE WE GET TO WORK

Stump grinding
questions.

Is stump grinding the same as stump removal?+

Grinding breaks down the agreed stump area rather than excavating the complete stump and root system. Roots outside the grinding area can remain. Tell us if your project requires excavation or specific site preparation so we can review the scope.

Are the wood chips hauled away?+

That depends on the agreed estimate. Let us know if you want the grindings left onsite or removed. Topsoil, grading, sod, and other restoration are not automatically included.

Can you reach a stump in a fenced backyard?+

Access needs to be reviewed for each job. Send the gate opening measurement and photos of the entire route, including turns, steps, and slopes. We will confirm whether the proposed equipment can reach the stump.

Can I get an estimate for several stumps?+

Yes. Send a count and measurements for each stump, along with photos and your ZIP code. We will review them together and confirm pricing after checking the job details.
